PANDORA PAPERS TEASER

By: Latashia Naidoo | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A new international leak of millions of documents into illicit offshore funds, known as the Pandora Papers, has just been revealed globally. Carte Blanche has the exclusive

Unique Selling Point:
IN NOVEMBER 2020, the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) obtained what’s now been recognised as the largest global leak of confidential financial documents pertaining to questionable investments linked to 14 offshore firms.

Carte Blanche has the South African exclusive.

Summary:
The Pandora Papers will become public knowledge on October 3, 2021, at 2pm (GMT), when simultaneously, more than 600 journalists from 117 countries will publish/broadcast their individual findings exposing financial chicanery, political corruption, and other evidence obtained from months-long investigations into a cache of 11.9 million leaked documents.

Pandora is the largest journalistic collaboration in the world, and the most extensive leak and subsequent investigation (thus far) into the shadowy world of offshore finance.

For my story on the Pandora Papers – as a prelude to the Cradle City investigation – I have obtained the following:
- A style guide created by the ICIJ for the project, including Pandora Papers logos, backgrounds, fonts, and imagery;
- Videos of behind-the-scenes footage of investigations in global newsrooms, as well as an interview with lead investigators on the project and the ICIJ director;
- Data maps and animations relevant to the global investigations;
- Verified data of celebrities and politicians implicated in the leaks, including: supermodel Claudia Schiffer, Kenyan president Uhuru Kenyatta, Sir Elton John, Columbian singer Shakira, Russian president Vladimir Putin and his mistress, among others;
- An explainer as to how this document leak differs from the Panama Papers and Paradise Papers, respectively;
- Details of verified analysts who have collaborated on this project and who will be able to provide financial analysis/details about the Pandora Papers, the scope of financial crimes, etc;
- I also have nine months worth of personal research and data, though I’m not sure how we can visually translate this into something watchable.

Press Release:


* Through a jaw-dropping leak of millions of documents, we join a global investigation into the sprawling, secretive industry of offshore systems that the world's rich and powerful use to hide assets and skirt tax rules by setting up front companies in far-flung jurisdictions and tax havens.

· It’s a new global leak of millions of documents which reveal an offshore financial system awash with trillions of dollars in dirty money. We join an international consortium of journalists exploring the secret files and expose the people behind the latest international leak of documents into illicit offshore funds.

· High-profile politicians, celebrities and heads of state implicated in dodgy financial dealings on a global scale. We join forces in analysing a jaw-dropping new cache of millions of documents into illicit offshore funds – getting the exclusive on what’s been recognized as the largest leak of confidential financial documents pertaining to questionable investments linked to 14 offshore firms.

· Why would more than 600 journalists from 117 countries collaborate to expose financial trickery, political corruption and evidence obtained from months-long investigations into a cache of 11.9 million leaked documents? We preview what is set to be the largest journalistic collaboration in the world, and the most extensive investigation so far into the shadowy world of offshore finance.

Script:


SCRIPT: PANDORA PAPERS TEASER – FINAL

COUNTDOWN: 03 October, 2021 - 12.30pm in Washington DC; 11.30am in Panama City, 5.30pm in London: 6.30pm in Paris; 6.30pm in South Africa.
GRAPHIC:
1 source
11.9 million leaked documents
2.94 TB of data
617 journalists representing 150 media outlets
VO: Tonight, at 6:30pm local time, an investigation by the biggest journalist collaboration in history into millions of leaked documents exposing international tax haven secrecy - broke globally.
And Carte Blanche has the South African exclusive.
VIZ: GRAPHIC: PANDORA PAPERS LOGO

VO: These are the Pandora Papers – a global investigation into the secret assets, covert dealings, and hidden fortunes of the world’s super-rich and powerful.

Gerard Ryle: [10:15:51] We're talking about presidents, we're talking about prime ministers. We're talking about rock stars. We're talking about porn stars and people that have been convicted of crimes all over the world. And what they're doing here is using this offshore secrecy to stop the crimes and to hide their crimes from governments and from the people.

VO: Gerard Ryle is the director of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists, the outfit leading the global investigative collaboration into the Pandora Papers.

GRAPHIC TO INCLUDE: HEADING: ICIJ-led investigation into 14 offshore firms.
1. All About Offshore (Seychelles) Limited - AABOL, based in the Seychelles
2. Alemán, Cordero, Galindo & Lee – ALCOGAL -Panamanian law firm - 1,956,478 files
3. Alpha Consulting Ltd - ALPHA
4. AsiaCiti Trust, based in Singapore: 1,823,788 files
5. Commonwealth Corporate Services Ltd / CCS Trust Limited - CCSL
6. CitiTrust, thought to be based in the Bahamas: 57,938 files
7. Commence BVI, based in BVI: 14,008 files
8. Demetrios A. Demetriades LLC, or DADLAW as it is commonly known, is a Cypriot law firm.
9. Fidelity Corporate Services Ltd - Fidelity
10. Glenn D. Godfrey & Company LLP - GDG
11. OMC Group
12. SFM Corporate Services, based in Dubai: 238,592 files
13. Trident Trust, based in the BVI: 671,522 files
14. IL Shin, or IL Shin Corporate Consulting Limited, a Korean provider based in Honk-Kong. About 800,000 files.

VO: An anonymous source shared with ICIJ 2.94 terabytes of confidential financial records, amounting to more than 11.9 million documents, from 14 offshore service providers that set up and manage shell companies and trusts in tax havens around the globe.
Gerard Ryle: [10:31:21] Shell companies are essentially the getaway vehicles for crime in the offshore world. We're not looking at a couple of million dollars here, we're looking at trillions of dollars. It's an entire ecosystem that we're looking at.

VIZ: POWERPLAYERS GRAPHIC

VO: The documents also feature a global cast of fugitives, oligarchs, celebrities, football stars and others, whose business dealings in tax and secrecy havens – whether legitimate or not - have now been uncovered.

VO: In short, the Pandora Papers have now laid bare the once-safely guarded offshore financial dealings of the mega rich and famous – for all the world to see.

VO: Some of the world’s well-known offshore hubs include Switzerland, Bermuda, the British Virgin Islands, and Cyprus. The US has also emerged as as a busy offshore destination in the new leaks.

VO: But why should the public – and especially the average South African – care about this data leak? Well for starters, there are 56 493 South African links to offshore entities which appear in the data. And while investing one’s money offshore in this way isn’t necessarily illegal, it does beg the question as to why a local business or entity would seek to store their wealth in an overseas tax haven?

VO: Rachel Etter-Phoya is a Malawian-based Senior Researcher for the Tax Justice Network. She says that the easy movement of illicit money through offshore firms and shell companies have devastating financial implications on economies – including South Africa.

RACHEL ZOOM:

We’re seeing yet again how Africa’s wealth is being moved out of the continent, how the most powerful elites and their politically-connected companies play by a completely different set of rules, at our expense.

VIZ:RACHEL ZOOM

00:03:06:12 - 00:03:14:07
>
But what is a tax haven? I think it's quite important that you understand it and why countries or states would choose to become tax havens. What does it mean for them?
00:03:15:18 - 00:03:48:02
>
So a tax haven in assets specializes in enabling people and companies to hide their wealth and financial affairs, it help them to escape the rules of the country that they're living. And as the name implies, it's often done or used as a way to underpay taxes. But that isn't all. It's also used by people who are trying to launder the money they've acquired through criminal activity, such as stealing state resources or through arms trade through drug trafficking.

VO: The Pandora Papers follows on the heels of similar massive document leaks into the world of tax havens and complex offshore financial structures. Most notably, the Panama Papers which were released in April 2016.
VIZ: YOUTUBE ICIJ FOOTAGE – CREDIT ICIJ: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fiu-vWLTqWs&t=50s

VO: There was even a movie about it – The Laundromat – starring Meryl Streep, and directed by Steven Soderbergh. https://youtu.be/wuBRcfe4bSo

VO: Then came the Paradise Papers in 2017, another global investigation into the offshore activities of some of the world’s most powerful people and companies in Bermuda and beyond. https://media.icij.org/uploads/2017/11/Latm-roundup-1400w-1-e1511303461164.png

VO: The Pandora Papers have also revealed secrets about politicians, business leaders, multinational corporations and criminals across Africa, who’ve all amassed wealth through shell companies.


VIZ RACHEL ZOOM:

>
So shell companies allow people to set up an anonymous company is another word, another way they've been called up those companies and they typically use not for actually carrying out business, but to arrange a financial affair so a company may be set up to own another company or assets. Bank account got a whole chain, may be arranged and makes it really difficult to follow the money, but got it in and of themselves are not illegal. And the problem isn't with setting up a company or even setting up an offshore company. It's the secrecy that we're still allowing some countries to offer the secrecy.

VIZ: WILL ZOOM

VO: Will Fitzgibbon is a senior journalist for the ICIJ, 00:00:41:01 - 00:01:08:25
ICIJ obtained the Pandora Papers – almost 12 million documents, almost two years now. And ever since then, we’ve been doing what ICIJ does best, which is both reporting on these documents to identify crucially important stories of public interest.

VO: The nearly-12 million documents range from passport photos, to financial statements, emails, and even video and audio recordings.

VIZ: WILL ZOOM:
00:01:55:17 - 00:02:37:20
The reason why these investigations take so long is that let's be honest today, criminals and people who use offshore companies who aren't criminals know that they shouldn't put everything in writing. It's very rare in my experience for a corrupt oil minister to write, Dear friends, please help me steal $10 million. That just doesn't happen. So journalists spend months and months speaking to experts, analyzing documents, understanding how the offshore system works in order to produce and publish stories that expose just how this dark money financial system causes harm to countries around the world.

LINK: CARD 2: AA623601.MXF 00:00:27:15 - 00:00:58:06 (NEEDS OVERLAY)
This is how tax evasion through offshore firms, works say, for example, you've got a 50 foot yacht docked in the south of France, but because you're a corrupt government official who shouldn't be able to afford such a luxury in the first place, you don't want anybody to know it belongs to you. So instead of the yacht being registered under your name, it can be bought and registered under the name of the shell company that's been created for you and the offshore tax haven of your choice. Now, if someone wants to find out who owns your yacht, it'll be virtually impossible.

VIZ: USE SNIPPETS

VO: While having an off shore company is not in itself illegal, Sir Elton John, singer Shakira, and even Beatle’s legend Ringo Starr are among the bold-faced names that the Pandora Papers have been able to link to shell companies.

VIZ: POWERPLAYERS GRAPHIC: (OVERLAY WITH THE GRAPHICS OF EACH PERSON IN POWERPLAYERS LINK)

VO: Media partners the Guardian, the BBC, and others are also investigating links of offshore investments and shell companies related to the likes of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s alleged mistress, the King of Jordan, former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair, and even Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta.

VO: But that’s just the tip of the iceberg.

VIZ: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fiu-vWLTqWs&t=52s (USE SNIPPETS)

VO: Tax revenue keeps civilization afloat. But not all taxpayers play by the same set of rules. With the help of a network of lawyers, accountants and complicit governments, the super wealthy and well-connected have often legally avoided paying trillions of dollars in taxes through their offshore investments. Which is why leaks like the Pandora Papers are so important for accountability.

CARD 2 - AA621501.MXF - 00:00:03:07 - 00:00:31:09

Link: According to Greek mythology, Pandora was gifted a box by the gods, which was told never to open. Now inside it contained all the world's evils, but curiosity got the best of Pandora, and when she opened, that box out poured all the evils into the world. But Pandora eventually did shut that box, and when she opened it once more, all that remained was hope. In the case of the Pandora papers, this hope is that the leak will spell a possible end for offshore tax havens.

Gerard Ryle: [10:19:21] I think there needs to be an international campaign against this. If there was a will to end this tomorrow, it could end. But when you have world leaders, when you have politicians, when you have public officials, all using the secrecy and all using this world, then I don't think we're going to see an end to it.

VO: Over the next few weeks, media partners around the globe - including the BBC, Radio France, Germany’s Süddeutsche Zeitung, and the Washington Post among others - will be breaking investigative stories about the rich and powerful who’ve been implicated in the Pandora Papers. And it’s just the beginning. Stay tuned to Carte Blanche over the next few weeks as we reveal the outcomes of months-long investigations into the sprawling, secretive industry of offshore systems.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A new international leak of millions of documents into illicit offshore funds, known as the Pandora Papers, has just been revealed globally. Carte Blanche has the exclusive
metadata.Unique Selling Point: IN NOVEMBER 2020, the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) obtained what’s now been recognised as the largest global leak of confidential financial documents pertaining to questionable investments linked to 14 offshore firms. Carte Blanche has the South African exclusive.
metadata.Summary: The Pandora Papers will become public knowledge on October 3, 2021, at 2pm (GMT), when simultaneously, more than 600 journalists from 117 countries will publish/broadcast their individual findings exposing financial chicanery, political corruption, and other evidence obtained from months-long investigations into a cache of 11.9 million leaked documents. Pandora is the largest journalistic collaboration in the world, and the most extensive leak and subsequent investigation (thus far) into the shadowy world of offshore finance. For my story on the Pandora Papers – as a prelude to the Cradle City investigation – I have obtained the following: - A style guide created by the ICIJ for the project, including Pandora Papers logos, backgrounds, fonts, and imagery; - Videos of behind-the-scenes footage of investigations in global newsrooms, as well as an interview with lead investigators on the project and the ICIJ director; - Data maps and animations relevant to the global investigations; - Verified data of celebrities and politicians implicated in the leaks, including: supermodel Claudia Schiffer, Kenyan president Uhuru Kenyatta, Sir Elton John, Columbian singer Shakira, Russian president Vladimir Putin and his mistress, among others; - An explainer as to how this document leak differs from the Panama Papers and Paradise Papers, respectively; - Details of verified analysts who have collaborated on this project and who will be able to provide financial analysis/details about the Pandora Papers, the scope of financial crimes, etc; - I also have nine months worth of personal research and data, though I’m not sure how we can visually translate this into something watchable.
